title: permanent_bipedal5 implementation
description:
Implement `permanent_bipedal5` over the F_5 packed type (T17), using `gray_code_iter` (T6) and `Packed5Vec::fold_mul`.

## Background

Mirrors the F_3 path: walk Gray-code subset order, update the packed column-sum vector by a single `Packed5::add`/`sub` per step, fold via the F_5 multiplication tree at each step. The function lives in `gf2-algebra::permanent::permanent_bipedal5`.

The lane-count of `Packed5` (chosen by R1) determines the matrix-size limit before multi-word streaming kicks in. Document that limit clearly.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] [hard] `gf2-algebra::permanent::permanent_bipedal5(matrix: &Packed5Matrix) -> Fp<5>` exists.
- [ ] [hard] Matrix-size upper bound for the single-word path is documented in the function doc-comment, and matches `Packed5::LANES`.
- [ ] [hard] Output bit-identical to `permanent_ryser<Fp<5>>` (T7) on 1000 random matrices for each $n \in \{1, \ldots, 14\}$ — covers epic success criterion 6.
- [ ] [hard] No `unsafe` in the gf2-algebra path.
- [ ] [hard] `cargo nextest run -p gf2-algebra --release --profile ci` passes.

## Amendment 2026-05-14 (user-approved — n=63/64 boundary infeasibility)

CLAUDE.md:149 prescribes word-boundary coverage at `0, 1, 63, 64, 65 bits` for primitives that allocate storage in `u64` words. For `permanent_bipedal5(matrix: &Packed5Matrix)`, a literal positive cross-check at `n = 63` or `n = 64` would require walking `2^n - 1` Gray-code subsets — `2^63 ≈ 9.2 × 10^18` and `2^64 ≈ 1.8 × 10^19` steps respectively, both physically infeasible (decades of single-thread CPU time even at one cycle per step). The Ryser oracle (`permanent_ryser<Fp<5>>`) is `O(n · 2^n)` as well and has the same wall-clock cost.

The single-word boundary is therefore covered as follows, in lieu of literal `n ∈ {63, 64}` positive cross-checks:

- **n = 0** — Vacuous-product = 1, covered by `test_permanent5_empty_matrix`.
- **n = 1** — Trivial single-lane path, covered by `test_permanent5_1x1`.
- **n = 65** — Panic at `Packed5::LANES = 64` boundary, covered by `test_permanent5_panics_on_n_65`.
- **n ∈ {15, 16}** — Slow-tier 1000-matrix cross-checks at `test_cross_check_n15` / `test_cross_check_n16` (exceed the criterion-required `n ∈ {1, …, 14}` range while still feasible).
- **n ∈ {20, 24, 32}** — Slow-tier sparse-batch cross-checks at `test_boundary_cross_check_n20` (20 matrices), `test_boundary_cross_check_n24` (10), and `test_boundary_cross_check_n32` (1). `n = 32` is the largest matrix dimension where a single random cross-check completes within the 120 s slow-tier budget; `n ≥ 33` exceeds it.

Per-lane storage-word correctness at the `bit 63 / bit 64 / bit 65` BitVec-level boundary is already covered by the `Packed5` / `Packed5Vec` type's own word-boundary tests at `crates/gf2-algebra/src/packed/packed5.rs` (committed in W4 sub-4a, issue `6917eb85`). `permanent_bipedal5` only consumes `Packed5` via its trait surface and inherits that coverage.

Approved by user 2026-05-14 (epic ae82bd73 session 8, AskUserQuestion option C: "Amend 684a6715 to document the infeasibility").
